title: If you're trying to use AI to trade, don't think of it as building one trading bot.
originalTitle: Don't build an AI trading bot, build three layers

recreating.summary: @max_kelleyy · "Don't build an AI trading bot, build three layers" · 8,561 likes and 5,021 comments on a 14K-follower account

length: about 35s at Joshua's pace, calm and close to the camera (the original is 34.6s) · Presenter: Joshua

lines.text: If you're trying to use AI to trade, don't think of it as building one trading bot.
Think of it as three layers that need to integrate and work together.
It's going to be this repo.
Layer 2 is going to be the agentic framework.
And the third layer is going to be the data layer.
I would start with these three tools in paper trading, test out a few different strategies, and see how they perform.
comment AI and I'll send you over the repo links plus a setup guide.

notes: **Recreating:** @max_kelleyy · https://www.instagram.com/p/DZsAke9RXxu/ · copy its rhythm: only five real visual changes, one every 5–7s (label off → screen 1 → screen 2 → screen 3 → face). Layer 1's screen cuts in on "Claude". Layers 2 and 3 cut in on the first words of their line ("Layer two", "And the third layer") and hold the whole line, like the original. Low-effort look on purpose: selfie held low and close, deadpan, phone pointed at a real monitor. No B-roll, no fast cuts, no punch-ins, no music hits.

**Layout:** full frame the whole way. Selfie full frame, or the phone-filmed monitor full frame (A2–A5), never split screen. Captions like the original: 2 lines, 4–6 words at a time, Inter Bold white with a soft black shadow, centred over his face (house preset "TQX Captions", set to 2 lines). Spell Qube and Claude exactly.
**Times** are estimates at Joshua's pace (3.2 words a second, about 35s). Re-time to the real take.

notes: **Presenter:** Joshua. One person, one list, in video order.
**Before recording anything:** the Qube team connects Claude to Qube on Joshua's laptop and gives him a Qube login. Don't show any install commands, API keys, emails, file paths or account details.

**The look:** every screen clip is filmed with Joshua's phone pointed at his monitor, handheld, like the original. Not a screen recording. Before each one: monitor brightness full, room lights on, wipe the screen, close every other window, hide the taskbar or dock, turn notifications off.
**Recording order for the screen clips** (one run, they build on each other): A2 → A4. A3 and A5 can be filmed any time.

rows.how: 1. Phone vertical (9:16), front camera, held in his hand at chest height and tilted up at his face (low and close, like the original). 2. At his desk, ceiling light on, lock focus and exposure on his face. 3. Record the hook twice, calm and deadpan. 4. Record lines 1–6 in one take, same calm voice, no pauses between lines. 5. Record the whole script once more, start to finish. The editor uses his voice the whole way and lays the screen clips over it.

1. CapCut text box, top left, 60px from the left and top edges. 2. Box red #EF4444, 16px rounded corners, 24px padding. 3. Two lines, Inter Bold 56px, white: line 1 `DO NOT build an` · line 2 `AI TRADING BOT`. 4. On from frame 1, off at 5.3s (on "Think"), no animation.

1. Terminal app, dark theme, font size 22, full screen. 2. Type `claude`, press Enter. Wait until Claude is ready. 3. Start filming the monitor with the phone, vertical, handheld, the Claude window filling the frame. 4. Type exactly, by hand, don't paste: `Build me a strategy in Qube. Buy the S&P 500 when it drops 2% or more in a day. Sell once it's up 2% from where I bought, or if it falls another 3%. Then test it on the last five years.` 5. Press Enter. 6. Keep filming until Claude says it has sent the strategy to Qube. Hold 3s. **CHECK: no email, key, file path or account name anywhere in the frame. If the setup shows one, stop and ask the Qube team to hide it.** **CHECK: Claude's reply must say the strategy went to Qube. If it doesn't, stop and send Mark a photo.**

rows.how: 1. Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing, logged out (a private window works). 2. Open https://www.tqx.ai/igqube2. 3. Film the monitor with the phone, vertical, handheld: the top of the page, Qube logo and headline in the middle of the frame. Hold 3s. **CHECK: the page's sample backtest (+55.43%, 814 trades) must not be in the frame. If it's in the way, film higher up the page.**

1. In Qube, open the strategy Claude sent over in A2. 2. Run the backtest on the last five years. 3. Film the monitor with the phone, vertical, handheld: the result screen, hold 2s. 4. Open the list of every trade and scroll slowly from the top, about 4s. **CHECK: the dates must cover five years or less (Qube tests on up to five years of real price data). If Qube runs longer, tell Mark before the edit.** **CHECK: no email or account name on screen. Don't change any number Qube shows; nothing from the result is said out loud.** 5. Photograph the result screen so the editor can copy the start date, end date and trade count exactly.

1. Open the broker app or web page Mark picks (see Still open). If it has a paper trading mode, switch it on. 2. Open the screen where you place an order (buy or sell ticket), with no order filled in. 3. Film it with the phone, vertical, handheld, the order screen filling the frame. Hold 6s. **CHECK: every account number, name, email, balance and the broker's logo or name gets blurred in the edit. If any of them can't be blurred cleanly, don't use the clip.** If there's no broker screen to film: Pexels, search exactly `trading app order screen`, pick a clip with no logos, no brand names and no faces, 6s.

1. Text in the top third, 1080×640 box: `Paper trading = fake money, real market`, Inter Bold 48px, white, on #0B0F14 85%, 24px padding, 16px rounded corners, "fake money" in gold #E8B04B. Pops in on "paper trading" (about 27.2s), holds 2.5s. 2. Badge top-right, whole of line 5 (25.0–31.3s): `Paper trading · simulated results`, Inter Bold 32px, white on #0B0F14 85%.
